questions.prompt: A commit is already on the remote and must be undone. Which command keeps the shared history intact?
questions.explanation: `git revert` adds a new commit that undoes the change; `git reset` would rewrite history that others already have.

source.section: ## 5. Undo a commit that is already on the remote

questions.prompt: You committed on `main` instead of your feature branch and have not pushed. What is the note's first step?
options: `git branch feature/login-form`, a new branch pointing at the commit, then reset `main` back
questions.explanation: Create the branch at the current commit first (nothing is lost), then `git reset --hard HEAD~1` moves `main` back, then switch to the feature branch.

source.section: ## 3. You committed on the wrong branch (not pushed yet)

questions.prompt: After rebasing a branch you had already pushed, how do you push it?
questions.explanation: A rebase rewrites the pushed commits, so the push needs `--force-with-lease`, never plain `--force`.

source.section: ## 7. Bring your branch up to date with main

questions.prompt: You added a file to `.gitignore`, but Git still tracks it. What removes it from the index while keeping your copy?
questions.explanation: `.gitignore` only affects untracked files; `git rm --cached <file>` stops tracking it and leaves the file on disk.
